title: Turkey, prepackaged or deli, luncheon meat

content.title: About
content.content: Turkey deli meat is a ready‑to‑eat sliced product made from turkey, sold either in sealed packages or at the deli counter. It has a mild flavor, light pink color, and a tender texture, suitable for sandwiches, salads, and snacks.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Turkey contains less fat than traditional pork or beef lunch meats.
It is often chosen for diet plans because of its low calorie density.
The product can be smoked, boiled, or baked depending on the processing method.
In many countries it is marketed as “deli turkey” and used as a ham alternative.
Some varieties are fortified with B‑vitamins and zinc.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Turkey provides less saturated fat than many other processed meats, supporting heart‑healthy eating.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: A typical serving supplies about 20 g of complete protein, helping maintain muscle mass.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains niacin, vitamin B6 and folate, which are important for metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Provides zinc and selenium, nutrients that support immune function.

items.title: Low calorie count
items.content: One slice (≈30 g) contains roughly 45 kcal, making it convenient for weight control.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to turkey.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Certain brands add salt; people with hypertension should choose low‑sodium options.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Some products contain nitrites or other preservatives; those sensitive should avoid them.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Turkey deli meat works well in sandwiches, wraps, salads, and as a topping for omelets or pizza. It can be briefly warmed in a pan or microwave if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in the original packaging in the refrigerator at +2–+6 °C. Once opened, consume within 3–5 days. Freezing is possible for up to 3 months, though texture may change.
